title: Denorm-flip debug journal
content:
Context:
I started seeing a repeatable failure where a subset of long-context chat sessions collapse to garbage tokens after ~250 tokens when using the int8/FP8 mix experiments on the 80B model. Hosted pathway not impacted; repro is on Dedicated infra with the RP5 cluster (A100 80GB).

High-level symptom:
- Good output until token ~240. Then one token goes high-magnitude (1e38) and subsequent tokens are NaN/garbage.
- Happens only with model variants that use the new tiny-float (FP8-E4M3) path or aggressive layerwise int8 on MLPs. BF16 path is stable.
- Repro rate ~6/10 with seed fixed; increases with longer sequences.

Quick notes / reminder to self:
- Not OOM: GPU memory flat, no cudaOutOfMemory seen.
- Not scheduler: same pattern across 2 different serving processes.
- Seems hardware-sensitive: A100 PCIe visible in one rack had lower repro than A100-SXM in other rack.
- A crash dump shows huge exponent flip on an intermediate GEMM output before layernorm.

Commands I ran (repro harness):
- baseline: python ./tools/repro_chat.py --model checkpoints/80b_fp32.pt --quant none --seed 42 --context 2048 --outfile out.txt
- repro-int8: python ./tools/repro_chat.py --model checkpoints/80b_mlp-int8.pt --quant int8 --seed 42 --context 2048 --outfile out_int8.txt
- repro-fp8: PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_SANITY=1 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python ./tools/repro_chat.py --model checkpoints/80b_fp8.pt --quant fp8 --seed 42 --context 2048 --outfile out_fp8.txt 2>&1 | tee fp8.log
- per-layer trace (inserted logging in runtime): RUNTIME_TRACE_LAYERS=8,12,20 python ... (see runtime patch)

Interesting log snippets (fp8 run):
- [layer 12][attn-matmul] max=1.2345e+38 mean=7.2e+16 -> next op had NaN inputs
- WARN: kv-cache write: detected denormal? value=1.4013e-45 truncated->0
- runtime: kernel cuBLAS_WRAPPED_gemm: return=0 (success) but downstream had isfinite==false

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Denormal/underflow -> exponent flush/rounding issue in FP8 path. Some kernels convert to tinyfloat and the transition loses exponent info, producing Inf/NaN after accumulation.
2) Accumulation precision problem: int8 on MLP + FP8 on attention leads to mixed-precision accumulation overflow in cuBLAS (accum type config mismatch).
3) Path-dependent kernel choice: for certain sequence lengths we pick a fused kernel that doesn't apply the same numeric protections (saturation/clip) -> latent NaNs.
4) GPU microarchitecture bug or divergent compiler flags causing different handling of subnormals on SXM vs PCIe.

Experiments to isolate (results inline):
A) Flush-to-zero on/off:
- export TF_ENABLE_DENORM_FLUSH=1 (not standard; custom runtime env used) -> repro rate dropped to 1/10 but not eliminated.
- set MXCSR in CPU tests to flush denormals -> no change for GPU runs (confirms GPU-side).

B) Force accumulation to fp32 in GEMM:
- patched runtime to set computeType=FP32 for cuBLAS in suspect kernels; repro disappeared on 3/3 runs (good sign).
- perf regressed ~1.4x.

C) Increase FP8 scaling (scale-up small values before quantize):
- added per-channel scale clamp (min_scale=1e-3) -> reduced NaN frequency but changed logits distribution (small accuracy shift).

D) Disable per-token KV caching (write-through):
- still repros, so KV cache write is likely not root cause but maybe amplification point.

E) Hardware swap (A100->T4 ephemeral):
- T4 runs stable (lower perf but stable), suggests a hardware/kernel interaction.

Quick grep of code paths (notes):
- runtime/quant/pack8.cu: quantize_value uses frexpf-based exponent calc, rounding path different from earlier pack16.
- runtime/ops/fused_gemm.cu: uses different epilog that omits isfinite check for performance.
- serving/ops/cache_write.cc has a fast path that assumes no NaNs (assert stripped).

Open experiments to run next:
- Re-run with cuBLAS logging and enable FP exceptions to catch first Inf. (how-to: set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and use cuda-memcheck? try gdb on worker to catch NaN at instruction).
- Try patched runtime with explicit isfinite checks after GEMM epilog and force clamp to +/-1e30 to avoid propagation. Measure how many sequences hit clamped path.
- Microbench: create minimal repro kernel that converts fp32->fp8->accumulate->fp32 and check for denorm behavior across different GPUs.
- Try compile with different nvcc flags (ftz=on/off) and see difference.

Notes on potential mitigations (tradeoffs):
- Force fp32 accumulation for all fused MLP GEMMs: safe but perf cost. Workaround while root cause investigated.
- Add per-operator post-check (isfinite) and soft-clamp: inexpensive to insert in runtime; might hide latent bugs.
- Revisit quantization scales and calibration sets: avoid tiny scales that push values into denormal range.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add a lightweight isfinite clamp in fused_gemm epilog (PR draft started) (owner: Evan).
- [ ] Run micro-repro across 4 GPU types, collect binary traces (owner: me).
- [ ] Add telemetry for max_abs, fraction_of_denormals to telemetry pipeline to detect in-prod early (owner: SRE/observability).
- [ ] File hardware ticket if microbench shows divergent behavior on SXM (owner: Marta).

Random observations / hope this saves time later:
- The condition often coincides with a token that contains many repeated punctuation chars in the prompt (maybe sparse attention patterns amplify quant error).
- Repro more frequently when batch has heterogeneous sequence lengths (padding/compaction kernel differences).
- When we disable continuous batching (single request per kernel), repro drops slightly; batching allocator/compaction likely changes kernel shape and path.

Scratch logs (copied terminal bits):
> Layer 12 out max 1.2e38 -> NaN detected at layernorm->scale (backtrace...)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tools/repro_chat.py", line 321, in <module>
    run_session(args)
  File "./runtime/serving.py", line 213, in run_with_quant
    outputs = model.forward_batch(batch)
  File "./runtime/ops/fused_gemm.cu", line 88, in cuLaunchKernel
    // epilog no isfinite checks
RuntimeError: invalid value encountered in upstream op

Notes-to-self: commit the microbench harness, keep PR small, get basic clamp in before next deploy. Leave longer-term perf fix (mixed accum) as engineering project.

Related tickets/reads:
- ENG-1472 (internal) - "FP8 denorm/overflow in fused kernels"
- RFC: tiny-float design doc (internal link in Confluence) - check exponent handling notes
- PR 882 in runtime: initial fp8 support (my review comments inline).

End of journal entry.
